trial_court: Additional District Judge (Matrimonial Cases), Jammu, RP No. 116/2022
facts_of_case: Suit filed by Amit Sharma against Rakhee Sharma under Section 13 of the Jammu and Kashmir Hindu Marriage Act. Suit was initially dismissed as the adulterer was not impleaded. Review petition filed and matter remanded to trial court.

legal_principles.principle: A party must plead all grounds for divorce in the suit.
legal_principles.held: The plaintiff had not pleaded adultery as a ground for divorce in the case filed by the husband as is evident from the averments made in the suit.

legal_principles.principle: A court cannot strike out a case for non-joinder of a party respondent if the trial court did not consider it necessary to implead that party.
legal_principles.held: Indeed, it is also submitted that the trial court did not consider it necessary to implead the adulterer as party defendant in the suit.

legal_principles.principle: A court must decide the issue of cruelty independently, regardless of other grounds for divorce.
legal_principles.held: It is also pleaded that the issue of cruelty could be determined independently in view of what had been pleaded and irrespective of the issue of adultery framed by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: A court cannot apply a rule that is inconsistent with the provisions of another Act.
legal_principles.held: As the principal Act itself stood repealed, the rules framed under 1970 Rules could not apply to the suit filed under the Act of 1980.

outcome.final_order: Court set aside judgment and decree of trial court, requiring adulterer to be impleaded in the suit.

keywords: Jammu and Kashmir Hindu Marriage Act
